questions.prompt: State the average power formula for a sinusoidal AC circuit using rms quantities.
What is the power factor of an AC circuit?
questions.answer: The power factor is \(\cos\phi\), where \(\phi\) is the phase angle between voltage and current.

questions.prompt: What is the average power dissipated by an ideal inductor or ideal capacitor over a full cycle?
questions.answer: The average power is zero. Ideal inductors and capacitors store energy during part of the cycle and return it during another part.

questions.prompt: An AC circuit has \(V_{\mathrm{rms}}=120\,\mathrm V\), \(I_{\mathrm{rms}}=2.0\,\mathrm A\), and power factor \(0.80\). Find average power.
A series circuit has \(I_{\mathrm{rms}}=3.0\,\mathrm A\) and \(R=25\,\Omega\). Find average power.
questions.answer:
Only the resistance dissipates average power:
\[
P_{\mathrm{avg}}=I_{\mathrm{rms}}^2R=(3.0)^2(25)=225\,\mathrm W
\]

questions.prompt: A series circuit has \(R=30\,\Omega\) and \(Z=50\,\Omega\). Find the power factor.
A device draws \(5.0\,\mathrm A\) rms from a \(230\,\mathrm V\) rms supply at power factor \(0.70\). Find its average power and apparent power.
questions.answer:
Average power is
\[
P_{\mathrm{avg}}=VI\cos\phi=(230)(5.0)(0.70)=805\,\mathrm W
\]
Apparent power is
\[
S=VI=(230)(5.0)=1150\,\mathrm{VA}
\]

questions.prompt: A series LRC circuit has \(V_{\mathrm{rms}}=100\,\mathrm V\), \(R=20\,\Omega\), and \(Z=40\,\Omega\). Find \(I_{\mathrm{rms}}\), power factor, and average power.
Derive \(P_{\mathrm{avg}}=I_{\mathrm{rms}}^2R\) for a series LRC circuit from \(P_{\mathrm{avg}}=V_{\mathrm{rms}}I_{\mathrm{rms}}\cos\phi\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[
P_{\mathrm{avg}}=V_{\mathrm{rms}}I_{\mathrm{rms}}\cos\phi
\]
For a series circuit,
\[
V_{\mathrm{rms}}=I_{\mathrm{rms}}Z
\]
and
\[
\cos\phi=\frac{R}{Z}
\]
Substitute:
\[
P_{\mathrm{avg}}=(I_{\mathrm{rms}}Z)I_{\mathrm{rms}}\frac{R}{Z}
\]
so
\[
P_{\mathrm{avg}}=I_{\mathrm{rms}}^2R
\]

questions.prompt: The instantaneous voltage and current are \(v=V_0\cos\omega t\) and \(i=I_0\cos(\omega t-\phi)\). Show that the average power is \(V_{\mathrm{rms}}I_{\mathrm{rms}}\cos\phi\).
questions.answer:
Instantaneous power is
\[
p=vi=V_0I_0\cos\omega t\cos(\omega t-\phi)
\]
Use
\[
\cos A\cos B=\frac12[\cos(A-B)+\cos(A+B)]
\]
Then
\[
p=\frac{V_0I_0}{2}[\cos\phi+\cos(2\omega t-\phi)]
\]
The average of the double-frequency cosine over a cycle is zero, so
\[
P_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{V_0I_0}{2}\cos\phi
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{rms}}=V_0/\sqrt2\) and \(I_{\mathrm{rms}}=I_0/\sqrt2\),
\[
P_{\mathrm{avg}}=V_{\mathrm{rms}}I_{\mathrm{rms}}\cos\phi
\]
